question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: v none -> none, whatever t is (t is not inspected). This holds at every depth: a none element, field value, item or map value is returned as none even under a malformed or missing tree.

Otherwise, when t is none (or absent) -> throws. When t is a bool, number, text or list, or a map whose k is anything other than exactly the text union, record, tuple, list or map (absent, another kind such as json, i64, text, none, bytes, a different spelling or case) -> v unchanged. In particular json positions are never descended into, so a record inside a json value stays positional.

UNION (k = union): alts that is not a list (absent, none, text, map, number, bool) -> throws. EVERY element of alts is examined: a none element anywhere in alts -> throws. A NONE ALTERNATIVE is an element that is a map whose k is exactly the text none. When alts has exactly two elements and exactly one of them is a none alternative, the result is RESHAPE(v, the other element), in either position. In every other case (zero, one, three or more elements; two none alternatives; two non-none alternatives) -> v unchanged. A followed element that is not a map (a number, text, bool, list) therefore yields v by R2. A union of two non-none alternatives is never followed, so a list v under record-then-list stays a list CITED FIDELITY package — cli/lang/rust.mjs:337

RECORD (k = record): v not a list -> v unchanged (a map v, even one already keyed by the field names, passes through as it is). v a list: fields none or absent -> throws; fields a number or bool -> v unchanged; fields a list whose length differs from v's -> v unchanged (the entries are not examined, so a malformed entry does not throw). When the lengths are equal: a field entry that is not a list (none, number, bool, map) -> throws; otherwise the result is a map with, for the entry at position i with name N (its first element) and field tree F (its second element, absent reads as none; elements after the second are ignored), N -> RESHAPE(element i of v, F). An empty fields list with an empty v yields the empty map. Two entries with the same name: the later one's value is kept. Field names are ordinary map keys, including the empty text and names such as __proto__ or __t CITED FIDELITY package — cli/lang/rust.mjs:338

TUPLE (k = tuple): v not a list -> v unchanged. v the empty list -> the empty list (items is not read). v a non-empty list: items none or absent -> throws; items a number, bool or text -> every element unchanged; items a list -> element i becomes RESHAPE(element i, items[i]) when items has a map at position i, and stays unchanged when items has no element there (v is longer) or a non-map element (none, number, text, bool, list). The result has v's length — extra elements are kept, never dropped, and a v shorter than items stays short CITED FIDELITY package — cli/lang/rust.mjs:339

LIST (k = list): v not a list -> v unchanged. Otherwise every element x becomes RESHAPE(x, item); an absent or none item therefore throws on the first non-none element and is harmless for an empty list or an all-none list.

MAP (k = map): v not a map (a list, text, number, bool) -> v unchanged. v a map -> a map with exactly v's keys, the value at each key becoming RESHAPE(value, val); the key tree is never read. An absent or none val therefore throws on the first non-none value and is harmless for an empty map or an all-none map. Every key is an ordinary key, including __proto__ CITED FIDELITY package — cli/lang/rust.mjs:341

A throw anywhere aborts the whole call (no partial result). The throwing positions are exactly: R2 (t none at a non-none v), R3 (alts not a list; a none element in alts), R4 (fields none or absent at a list v; a non-list entry at equal lengths), R5 (items none or absent at a non-empty v), and R6 and R7 through R2.
